sections.heading: 3. History of Present Illness / Current Episode

paragraphs.label: Primary reason for treatment
paragraphs.text: The patient reports feeling down, crying almost every day, and no longer enjoying activities.

paragraphs.label: Duration of current episode
paragraphs.text: The patient reports the symptoms have been present for about three months, since losing their job in July.

paragraphs.label: Precipitating / contextual factors
paragraphs.text: The patient reports losing their job in July as a precipitating factor.

paragraphs.label: Functional impact
paragraphs.text: The patient reports waking up at four in the morning and not being able to get back to sleep, resulting in approximately five hours of sleep per night. The patient also reports a decreased appetite and weight loss of about ten pounds.

paragraphs.label: Narrative / additional details
paragraphs.text: The patient reports sometimes wishing they would not wake up but denies any suicidal ideation or plans. The patient has no history of prior psychiatric hospitalizations and has never attempted to harm themselves.

The patient reports experiencing persistent feelings of sadness and a lack of enjoyment in activities for the past three months. The patient also reports waking up at four in the morning and experiencing difficulty returning to sleep, resulting in approximately five hours of sleep per night. The patient notes a decrease in appetite and a weight loss of about ten pounds. The patient denies any current thoughts of harming themselves but acknowledges feeling that they do not want to wake up sometimes. The patient reports no prior psychiatric hospitalizations and minimal past mental health treatment, including one session of therapy in college. The patient's mother had depression and their uncle had a history of alcohol abuse. The patient stopped drinking alcohol a year ago and denies any other drug use. The patient is currently taking lisinopril for blood pressure. The patient expressed willingness to try sertraline fifty milligrams daily as recommended by the doctor.

paragraphs.text: The patient denies prior suicide attempts or self-harm.

The provider discussed starting sertraline fifty milligrams daily for the patient's depressive symptoms. The provider will see the patient again in two weeks. The provider decided not to prescribe any sleeping pills or benzodiazepines at this time. The provider discussed side effects such as nausea and headache with the patient and mentioned therapy as an alternative option.
